summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with fever and hypotension following a dialysis session, suspected to be due to a persistent infection of his tunneled femoral dialysis line. He was transferred from the ED to the ICU, started on vancomycin and gentamicin, and placed on vasopressor support. The infected line was removed on hospital day 2, and cultures confirmed MRSA bacteremia. After line removal, his blood pressure stabilized, vasopressors were weaned, and he completed a 'line holiday' while receiving IV vancomycin. A new tunneled dialysis catheter was successfully placed via the left external jugular vein on day 7. He remained afebrile with negative repeat blood cultures, and his heart function was reassessed with a TTE showing mild worsening. He was discharged home with services to continue six weeks of IV vancomycin during dialysis, with close monitoring of labs and follow-up with nephrology, infectious disease, and primary care.
